title: Sponsorship Agreement
subtitle: January 19–21, 2027

clauses.t: This Sponsorship Agreement (the “Agreement”) is between the Organizer and the Sponsor identified on the Sponsorship Information page (“Organizer” and “Sponsor”), and is effective on the date of the last signature below. It remains in effect until the No-CAP Workshop, to be held online January 19–21, 2027 (the “Workshop”), and delivery of the Sponsor Report described in Section 8 are complete.

In consideration of the Fee, Organizer will provide Sponsor the benefits set out in Exhibit A (Sponsor Benefits) for the Sponsorship Level selected on the Sponsorship Information page. Exhibit A is attached to and forms part of this Agreement.

Sponsor will pay the sponsorship fee for the Sponsorship Level selected on the Sponsorship Information page, as stated in Exhibit A (the “Fee”), by ACH, wire transfer, or check to the account on the invoice that Organizer will issue upon execution of this Agreement. Payment is due within thirty (30) days of the invoice date and in all cases no later than January 8, 2027. Sponsor is responsible for all taxes on the Fee other than taxes on Organizer’s income. If the Fee is not paid when due, Organizer may suspend Sponsor’s benefits and remove Sponsor’s logo from the Workshop website and opening cards until payment is received, and the Fee remains owed except as provided in Section 10.

Sponsor will deliver its logo (or, at levels that list a name only, its name) in an appropriate format and its website URL to Organizer no later than January 5, 2027. Organizer may resize the logo and place it in the forms required by the Workshop design. Materials received after that date will be used on a reasonable-efforts basis and may be omitted from opening cards, and the Fee is not reduced.

Sponsor grants Organizer a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Sponsor’s name, logo, and trademarks as provided by Sponsor solely to deliver the benefits under this Agreement and to promote the Workshop, including on opening cards, the Workshop website, emails, and recordings and transcripts. This license continues for recordings and archives that remain online after the Workshop. Organizer will cease new uses upon Sponsor’s request but is not required to alter materials already published or recordings already posted. All goodwill arising from use of Sponsor’s marks inures to Sponsor. Sponsor may describe itself as a sponsor of the No-CAP Workshop at its Sponsorship Level, may link to the Workshop website, and may use the Workshop name and the logo and graphics provided by Organizer for that purpose. Upon withdrawal or termination, Sponsor will cease new use of the Workshop name and graphics and new statements that it is a sponsor, except accurate historical references; the license granted to Organizer for materials and recordings already published continues.

Workshop leads, sessions, and scope are determined independently of sponsors by the Workshop’s Steering Committee under its published charter. Sponsorship does not entitle Sponsor to a session, a speaking slot, a seat or vote on the Steering Committee, a preview of session proposals, or any control over the content of any session or day. Sponsor’s personnel may submit proposals on the same terms as any other person and will be evaluated under the same published criteria. Any individual from Sponsor who leads a session must agree to the Workshop’s Lead Agreement.

The use of Sponsor’s name on the Workshop website or opening cards does not constitute endorsement by Organizer or the Steering Committee of Sponsor or of Sponsor’s products or services. Sponsor will not represent that the Workshop, Organizer, FedRAMP, or any government agency has endorsed Sponsor or its products or services. Organizer does not award exclusive sponsorships or establish exclusive relationships, and Sponsor will not imply that any such relationship exists. Organizer may have other sponsors at the same level.

Attendees are not required to register. Organizer will not provide Sponsor with attendee lists, contact information, or lead scans. Within {{report_days}} days after the Workshop, Organizer will provide Sponsor an aggregate report covering attendance numbers, participation and engagement, and a summary of attendee experience and key learnings, based on aggregate counts or estimates (the “Sponsor Report”). Organizer makes no representation as to attendance, audience size, reach, or business results.

Sponsor and its representatives will comply with the competition-law provisions of the Lead Agreement and the Steering Committee charter in connection with the Workshop, including by not agreeing on or exchanging information about prices, bids, customers, or markets. Organizer may immediately suspend or remove any Sponsor representative from the Workshop for harassment, disruption, or other violation of the conduct rules in the Steering Committee charter, with prompt written notice to Sponsor. Organizer may also immediately suspend Sponsor’s marks and benefits, on prompt written notice, for a serious or ongoing violation of this Section or Section 7; suspension is not termination and does not by itself forfeit the Fee. For any other breach of this Section that Sponsor does not cure within ten (10) days of written notice, Organizer may remove Sponsor’s marks and withhold remaining benefits, and the Fee will not be refunded.

(a) Sponsor may withdraw by written notice on or before January 8, 2027, in which case Organizer will refund any Fee paid and any unpaid Fee is no longer owed. After that date the Fee is non-refundable except as provided in this Agreement. (b) If Organizer cancels the Workshop, Sponsor may elect, within thirty (30) days of notice of the cancellation, a refund of the Fee paid or a credit in the same amount toward a future Workshop, and any unpaid Fee is no longer owed. (c) If the Workshop is postponed or moved, this Agreement continues for the new dates, and a Founding Sponsor’s Named Day becomes the corresponding day of the rescheduled Workshop; if the new dates are more than six (6) months after January 21, 2027, Sponsor may instead elect a refund. (d) If a Founding Sponsor’s Named Day is cancelled and not rescheduled, Organizer will offer Sponsor another day or a pro rata refund of the Fee, being one-third of the Fee. (e) If a material benefit listed in Exhibit A is not delivered for any reason other than Sponsor’s breach, request, or other act or omission (including a request under Section 5), Organizer will provide substitute delivery reasonably acceptable to Sponsor or refund a proportionate part of the Fee. (f) Organizer will pay each refund or issue each credit within thirty (30) days of the election or the event giving rise to it. (g) Each remedy under this Section or Section 13 reduces the total Fee once, by the amount of the refund or reduction due. The reduction is applied first against any unpaid part of the Fee, and Organizer will refund in cash only the amount by which the Fee paid exceeds the adjusted Fee.

Neither party will be in default to the extent that its performance is delayed or prevented by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, pandemic, war, government action, or an internet or platform outage. Where such an event prevents delivery of the benefits, Sponsor’s remedies are as stated in Section 10(b) through (e).

Organizer provides the benefits as described in this Agreement and makes no other warranty, express or implied. Neither party is liable to the other for indirect, special, or consequential damages or lost profits. Organizer’s total liability under this Agreement is limited to the Fee actually paid. Nothing in this Agreement limits liability that cannot be limited by law. Sponsor represents that it has the right to grant Organizer the license to the logos and materials it supplies.

Either party may terminate this Agreement if the other materially breaches it and fails to cure within thirty (30) days of written notice, subject to the refund provisions of Section 10. If Sponsor terminates for Organizer’s uncured material breach, Organizer will refund a proportionate part of the Fee for benefits not delivered. Sections 5, 7, 8, 12, and 15 survive termination or expiration.

The parties are independent contractors, and neither is the partner or agent of the other. Organizer may use staff and contractors to deliver the benefits and may assign this Agreement to a successor that operates the Workshop.

This Agreement, together with Exhibit A and the Steering Committee charter and the Lead Agreement, in the versions published on the Workshop website on the effective date, as they apply under Sections 6 and 9, constitutes the entire understanding of the parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions, and sponsorship summaries and prospectuses describe but do not modify it. In the event of conflict, this Agreement controls as to fees, benefits, termination, and refunds. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both parties. Notices under this Agreement may be given by email to the contacts on the signature page and are effective when sent. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of California, and the state and federal courts located in Alameda County, California have exclusive jurisdiction. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and electronically, including by exchange of signed PDFs.
